blocker.summary: r460 implemented RB_COLOR_MASK partial-write-mask support in PinnedShaderRuntime, named by r459's second track. Unlike r459's EDRAM-tile-under-MSAA question, the 4-bit-to-VkColorComponentFlags translation is mechanical and unambiguous (R=bit0..A=bit3, same order already used elsewhere in this file), so it was implemented directly. A live trace showed the real value encountered: RB_COLOR_MASK=0x0 (a draw that writes no color channel at all). PipelineKey extended with color_mask (like sample_count in r459) since colorWriteMask is static pipeline state here. Verified: native ctest 11/11, no regression, and a live probe against the real ISO confirms the rejection message is gone (0 occurrences) AND a real improvement: the fallback count dropped from 9 to 8 -- one previously-failing draw is now actually pinned (runs through execute_frame(), not the structural-validation fallback), consistent with a zero color mask writing no visible pixels by construction (non_black/distinct_colors unchanged, as expected). A new, unrelated, not-yet-investigated rejection surfaced once: 'render target region exceeds the bounded size'. Named for r461: (1) the pinned registry coverage gap (r456, now 7 of the remaining 8 fallbacks) likely needs an oracle session -- user decision, not to be spent unilaterally; (2) the new 'render target region exceeds the bounded size' rejection, surfaced once, not yet investigated -- could be a simple bound widening or a real coverage gap. Still open, non-blocking: once the wiring is judged mature, reconsider the backlog commit decision (r433/r434/r438/r454-r460); update tools/prepare.py/build.py to default to the current ISO path (r452/r453, convenience only).
